Deck maxim: "one retry edge beats one more agent".

Agents coordinate through shared state instead of direct messages.
The workspace may be a database, vector store, filesystem, Git repo or task graph.
Agents can join or leave without rewiring; shared state is durable and inspectable.
A pipeline localises errors; a blackboard localises state. Neither has a path backwards.
Agents propose and discuss, then a judge or vote resolves.
Failure mode: agreement without independence - the same model and context means the same blind spot.
Agents bid for announced tasks on capability, cost and latency, so work lands on the cheapest capable agent.
Bids: A100 $0.20 / 3s; T4 $0.05 / 10s; H100 $0.40 / 1s. "Cheapest bid under 5s wins" - the job goes to the A100 node.
Failure mode: bids are self-reported, so an agent can win by overstating what it can do.

slides.title: Communication: the vocabulary, and the semantics

elements.text: AGENT COMMUNICATION IS A DISTRIBUTED-SYSTEMS PROBLEM
Communication: the vocabulary, and the semantics
Structured control fields let the runtime act without asking an LLM what a message meant.
DELEGATE, QUERY, REPORT, HANDOFF, UPDATE, CANCEL, ACK, ERROR, COMPLETE.
A control message: id "msg-381", task_id "t-17", from "planner", to "researcher", type "DELEGATE".

Natural language - flexible but ambiguous.
Structured - easy to validate, less expressive.
A structured result message: task_id "T17", type "result", status "complete", confidence 0.82, evidence ["log:2391", "commit:X"], artifact "analysis/T17.json".
Scenario: "purchase 8 GPU instances"; network timeout, no reply. at-most-once vs at-least-once - "is exactly-once even available here?" Put an idempotency key on the task_id.
